advances: Counterexample to gluing whole endpoint bodies from globally critical proper captured-side equalities and a middle-plane cover. The normalized depth exceeds the planar sharp target, and the three-cap balance is only on the middle plane.

proof:
The defining inequalities give a compact full-dimensional convex body, with exactly three nonempty integer fibers. The area of $K_r$ is $(r^2-h^2)/2$. Substituting the three radii gives $M$, $\max_r|K_r|<Q$ and $M/2-\max_r|K_r|=53954/235225>0$. Averaging corresponding vertices $(h,0),(r,0),(0,r),(0,h)$ puts all vertices of $K_1$ in the endpoint midpoint. The reverse inclusion follows from the four fiber inequalities. The two endpoint edges with outward normal $(-1,-1)$ have equal positive lengths, so an endpoint homothety would have ratio one. The edges with outward normal $(1,1)$ have different lengths, excluding this possibility.

All displayed caps pass through $Y$, which is own-interior. With the first continuous normal written as $(-1,-1)$, the other two sum to $(4t-1)(1,1)$. The middle margins therefore have a positive linear dependence and their closed caps cover the entire middle plane. The first cap captures the same frustum $h\le x+y\le2t$ in the nonnegative quadrant on all three bases. Its area is $\delta$ since $h^2=12t^2-4t$ and $2t<1-\varepsilon$. The second cap captures the translate by $(\varepsilon z,0)$ of
$$
D=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,0),(4t-1,0),(1-2t,2t)\}
$$
at base $z$. In fact the constraints $y\ge0$, $x+y\le1+\varepsilon z$ and the second cap already give this translated triangle. The remaining inequalities $x\ge0$ and $x+y\ge h$ are slack there because $4t-1-\varepsilon>h$ and $1-2t-\varepsilon>0$. The area of $D$ is $2t(1-2t)$. Swapping $x,y$ proves the same claim for the third cap, with translates by $(0,\varepsilon z)$. This gives properness, exact trace midpoints and total cap areas $Q$.

For the all-direction lower bound at $Y$, translate each containing halfspace parallel to itself through $Y$. A pure-base cap retains the whole middle and one whole endpoint, of total area greater than $Q$ by the formulas above. For a nonvertical cap, swap the two continuous coordinates if needed so the first continuous coefficient has greatest absolute value. Its sign can be made positive by taking the opposite orientation. Nonvertical boundaries have area zero on each fiber, so it suffices to show both $P\ge Q$ and $P\le M-Q$ for the orientation with first coefficient $1$. The remaining continuous coefficient $k$ lies in $[-1,1]$, and the coefficient $\alpha$ of $z$ is unrestricted. Set $c_z=t(1+k)-\alpha z$. If $G_r(k,c)$ denotes the area of $\{x,y\ge0,\ x+y\le r,\ x+ky\ge c\}$, then the mixed cap area is
$$
P(k,\alpha)=\sum_{z=-1}^{1}\big[G_{1+\varepsilon z}(k,c_z)-G_h(k,c_z)\big].
$$
For $0<k<1$, similar triangles give the four consecutive formulas $r^2/2$, $r^2/2-c^2/(2k)$, $(r-c)^2/[2(1-k)]$, and $0$, at intervals separated by $0,kr,r$ in $c$. For $-1<k<0$ the four formulas are $r^2/2$, $r^2/2-(c-kr)^2/[2(-k)(1-k)]$, $(r-c)^2/[2(1-k)]$, and $0$, separated by $kr,0,r$. Adjacent formulas agree at the breaks. For $\alpha\ge2$ or $\alpha\le-2$ the endpoints have already saturated with one fully captured and one empty. It suffices to use the compact rectangle in $(k,\alpha)$ with $|\alpha|\le2$.

Here is the finite rational certificate. For $z=\pm1$ and $r\in\{1+\varepsilon z,h\}$, take the affine lines $\alpha=[t(1+k)-w]/z$ with $w\in\{0,kr,r\}$, together with $-2,2,-\varepsilon,0,\varepsilon$, removing duplicates. These are the 15 lines. For each of $[-1,0]$ and $[0,1]$, partition $k$ at their pairwise crossings, at roots of $t(1+k)=w$ for $w\in\{0,kr,r\}$ and $r\in\{1,h\}$, and additionally at $3-1/t$ in $[0,1]$. Include the interval endpoints. On each open interval $(l,r_*)$ the line order is fixed. Its 14 successive strips have lower and upper affine boundaries $L(k),U(k)$. The triangle branches are fixed on the open strip, determined at $k=(l+r_*)/2$ and $\alpha=(L(k)+U(k))/2$.

For each strip use the lower polynomial $2\operatorname{sign}(k)k(1-k)(P-Q)$ and the upper polynomial with $P-Q$ replaced by $M-Q-P$. Their multiplier is strictly positive in the open strip. Substitute $k=l+(r_*-l)v$, $\alpha=L(k)+(U(k)-L(k))u$. If the resulting polynomial is $\sum_{p,q}c_{pq}v^p u^q$ of separate degrees $N,D$, its tensor Bernstein coefficients are
$$
b_{ij}=\sum_{p\le i,\ q\le j}
 c_{pq}\frac{\binom i p}{\binom N p}\frac{\binom j q}{\binom D q}.
$$
The basis polynomials $\binom N i v^i(1-v)^{N-i}\binom D j u^j(1-u)^{D-j}$ are nonnegative on the unit square. The coefficient identity follows by expanding each monomial in the Bernstein basis using the binomial theorem. For the zero polynomial use coefficient zero. Every entry is nonnegative. The original area inequalities extend to all strip boundaries and $k=-1,0,1$ by dominated convergence, since the nonvertical boundary has area zero on each fixed fiber. The exact coefficient data and a regenerating script are in [the archived certificate](../assets/pk-nov6/computations/truncated_triangle_exact_bernstein_certificate.json) and [its verifier](../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_truncated_triangle_globalcritical_cap_gluing.py).

It follows that every containing halfspace at $Y$ has area at least $Q$. The three displayed caps attain that mass and cover the middle plane. Each outer point belongs to an endpoint-isolating pure-base cap of mass below $Q$. Thus the global maximum is $Q$, and $Q/M=182000000/405433227$. The endpoint nonhomothety concerns whole bodies, even though the pieces for each separate cap are translates.

statement:
Set $h=20/97$, $t=100/291$, $\varepsilon=1/100$, $\delta=2t(1-2t)$ and $Q=3\delta=18200/28227$. Let
$$
C=\{(z,x,y):-1\le z\le1,\ x,y\ge0,\ h\le x+y\le1+\varepsilon z\}.
$$
The three actual integer fibers are the truncated triangles $K_{1-\varepsilon},K_1,K_{1+\varepsilon}$, where $K_r=\{(x,y):x,y\ge0,\ h\le x+y\le r\}$. The middle fiber is the Minkowski average of the endpoints, and the endpoints are nonhomothetic. The closed ambient caps
$$
\begin{aligned}
x+y&\le2t,\\
tx+(3t-1)y-\varepsilon tz&\ge t(4t-1),\\
(3t-1)x+ty-\varepsilon tz&\ge t(4t-1)
\end{aligned}
$$
are through $Y=(0,t,t)$, cover the entire middle plane, and are proper in each of the three fibers. For each cap the captured endpoint bodies are translates, their Minkowski average equals the captured middle body, and all three traces have area $\delta$. The maximum raw mixed halfspace depth is exactly $Q$, attained at $Y$, so these caps are critical there. The total mixed area is $M=135144409/94090000$, and each fiber has area less than both $M/2$ and $Q$. In particular this proper source-plane equality cover does not imply endpoint homothety.
title: A globally critical proper cap cover with nonhomothetic endpoints
